newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian 1996 budget deficit to be increased.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian 1996 budget deficit to be increased.

text.p: Lithuania's new right-wing government wants to boost the 1996 budget deficit by some 400 million litas and plans to present the draft 1997 budget in 10 to 15 days, politicians said on Wednesday.

"The budget committee intends to provide the draft budget for 1997 in 10 to 15 days," Elvyra Kunaviciene, budget and finance committee head, told journalists. She added that she hoped the budget for 1997 would be passed this year.
Kunaviciene gave no figures for the 1997 budget, but budget committee vice-chairman Kasputis Glavacaskas said changes would be made to the areas where taxes are levied.
He said investments should not be taxed and that the budget would aim to boost the capital market.
He said the committee wanted to decrease the burden of income tax and levy more taxes on real estate, which he said would boost peoples' purchasing power.
Kunaviciene also said the 1996 deficit had to be raised because revenue collection had fallen short. The current planned deficit is 704 million litas.
"The deficit of the (1996) budget should be increased by 430 million litas," Kunaviciene said.
She said the old ex-Communist government failed to collect 320 million litas in VAT, 230 million litas in excise tax, 100 million litas company tax and 86 million litas income tax.
She said the current 704 million litas deficit had already been reached.

Lithuania's right-wing coalition dominated by the Homeland Union Party of independence leader Vytautas Landsbergis aims, as its primary goal right now, to revise this year's budget and determine the state's financial situation.
